sentences.text: The Meridian region is a dense aviation service area with a primary international hub, several high-frequency domestic airports, and multiple cargo and general aviation aerodromes operating within shared terminal airspace.
Traffic demand is concentrated in two daily peaks driven by banked airline schedules, regional commuter waves, express freight departures, and time-sensitive connections to long-haul services.

The airport network routinely operates near declared capacity during Normal Operations, leaving limited margin for runway configuration changes, surface congestion, or short-notice airspace constraints.
Congestion is amplified because arrivals to the main hub and departures from nearby secondary airports use common fixes and adjacent climb corridors.
Seasonal thunderstorms, coastal fog, strong crosswinds, and convective reroutes frequently reduce the effective Airport Acceptance Rate across the network.
Military training areas and special-use airspace also create recurring sector loading constraints that require close coordination with the Military Airspace Liaison.
Surface constraints at the busiest airports include limited gate buffers, intersecting taxi routes, constrained remote stand access, and uneven availability of ground handling resources.
When these constraints combine, local decisions made at one airport can quickly create airborne holding, missed departure opportunities, and uneven delay distribution across the Meridian region.

The operational mission is to provide a shared air traffic flow management and airport collaborative decision-making capability that aligns network demand, airport capacity, and surface readiness before congestion becomes unstable.
The Regional Flow Manager is the lead operational actor for balancing demand against capacity across the Meridian region and for coordinating regional traffic management actions.

The Airline Operations Coordinator, Aircraft Operator Representative, Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, and Slot Coordinator require a common basis for decisions rather than separate local views of the same operational picture.
The Regional Flow Platform is intended to integrate planning, tactical regulation, airport readiness, and post-event analysis into a single operational environment.
The Demand Prediction Service estimates expected demand from scheduled operations, Flight Intent Message data, known airline recovery plans, and near-term operational changes.
The Capacity Assessment Module supports the assessment of declared and tactical capacity using weather, runway availability, sector loading, and airport resource conditions.
The Slot Allocation Engine supports fair and traceable allocation of constrained departure and arrival opportunities when demand exceeds available capacity.
The Airport CDM Portal provides airport stakeholders with a controlled interface for sharing operational readiness information and confirming decisions that affect the surface and terminal sequence.

The Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, and Arrival Regulation Console support the transition from regional planning decisions to executable airport and tower actions.
The Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Airline Interface Adapter provide the data feeds needed to maintain a current and consistent operational picture.

The Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, and West Apron Sensor provide additional indicators of emerging capacity loss and operational imbalance.
The Common Situation Display is expected to give authorized users a shared view of demand, capacity, constraints, and active traffic management measures.
The Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger are expected to preserve the rationale, timing, and authorization of material operational decisions.

During Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State, the system must support rapid development of a Tactical Regulation Proposal and consistent communication of the resulting Ground Delay Program when one is required.
During Recovery Phase, the system must help stakeholders restore scheduled flow while monitoring Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, and Slot Compliance State performance.

The mission need is therefore a resilient, governed, and interoperable capability that reduces avoidable delay, improves predictability, and enables transparent collaboration across the Meridian airport network.
